purpose: Collect sequence-separated, fixed-read group-deletion outcomes for testing whether source early features predict conditional token utility. This is a diagnostic, not a new inference selector or full-video experiment.
read_selection: Use the pre-existing fixed capture frames only. Require verified source attribution and exactly 5120 attributed historical non-conditioning keys with source frame strictly less than current frame minus one; exclude and report reads that do not meet this requirement. Protect conditioning memory, the newest source, unattributed keys, and the object-pointer tail.
intervention: For each eligible read, order eligible keys by their original attention position, then partition them into five disjoint groups of 1024 using a deterministic pseudorandom permutation seeded from SHA-256 of the fixed protocol identifier, sequence and target frame. Replay one no-op and five arms that remove one group each, preserving all remaining original memory and position order. All deletion arms remove exactly 1024 keys and have identical attention-key count. No-op is an extra-key reference, not a matched-key arm. Save group membership, hashes and output masks before evaluating any target label.
features: Any future group descriptor must be computed only from source-frame early features, automatic prompt/predicted masks, source coordinates, inference-available usage and optional RGB, with aligned pooling defined and audited before fitting. The current protocol does not define or train a selector, choose groups using labels, or modify the live model.
evaluation: After masks and group identities are frozen, compare each group deletion with the no-op using Dice on labeled-present frames and false-alarm status on labeled-empty frames. The difference is conditional on the other keys and attention renormalization. Report all arms, distribution and eligible/excluded reads, not only selected effects. Assess any learned selector on held-out sequences with RGB, shuffled, usage and distributed controls under matched key counts before considering video propagation.
verification: Require source identity audit, exact no-op attention and decoder outputs and original binary mask, fixed group coverage and disjointness, preserved pointers and conditioning/newest spans, saved file hashes, deterministic independent repeat and independently scored target masks. Development sequences may guide design; validation sequences are sequence-separated, not proven patient-independent. Priority sequences remain untouched by this data collection.
constraints: Automatic YOLO prompt and existing Lean inference are unchanged; no redetection, new confidence threshold, or ground-truth-derived inference input. No efficacy or generalization claim follows from local deletions. Store experiment artifacts only in the authorized Google Drive experiment directory.
